PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 32 years
Sample Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Abnormal ultrasound findings at 11 weeks gestation

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Analysis of uncultured chorionic villi using polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. QF-PCR was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for STR markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak areas were calculated and dosage ratios determined for informative markers.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 18: ABNORMAL - TRISOMY 18 DETECTED
Eight informative markers demonstrated triallelic patterns or abnormal dosage ratios consistent with trisomy:
- D18S976 (18p11.31): Triallelic pattern 1:1:1
- D18S1002 (18q11.2): Diallelic ratio 2:1
- D18S819 (18q11.2): Triallelic pattern 1:1:1
- D18S847 (18q12.1): Diallelic ratio 2:1
- D18S535 (18q12.3): Triallelic pattern 1:1:1
- D18S978 (18q12.3): Diallelic ratio 2:1
- D18S386 (18q22.1): Triallelic pattern 1:1:1
- D18S390 (18q22.3): Diallelic ratio 2:1

CHROMOSOME 13: NORMAL
All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns

CHROMOSOME 21: NORMAL
All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns

SEX CHROMOSOMES: XY (MALE)
AMELOGENIN: X:Y ratio 1:1
SRY: Present
X-linked markers: Single allele patterns consistent with male karyotype

CONCLUSION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates TRISOMY 18 (Edwards syndrome) in this male fetus. The findings are concordant with the abnormal ultrasound features observed at 11 weeks gestation.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
Edwards syndrome (Trisomy 18) is associated with severe intellectual disability and multiple congenital anomalies including cardiac defects, clenched hands with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, and growth restriction. The prognosis is poor with most affected infants dying within the first year of life.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Follow-up karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and exclude mosaicism
2. Genetic counseling should be offered to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
3. Detailed ultrasound examination to assess fetal anomalies
4. Discussion of pregnancy management options

LIMITATIONS
- QF-PCR cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Segmental chromosomal imbalances outside the regions tested will not be detected
- Maternal cell contamination can affect results, though no evidence was seen in this case

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
